system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

In the case where the user information is encoded using the GSM 7 bit default alphabet and the last character terminates at an octet boundary, this parameter indicates the number of octets of user information. [FCC-HI-2018#0053] Report and Recommendations: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency January 13, 2018 False Alert (p.11):
8:05 a.m. HI-EMA’s midnight shift supervisor begins a no-notice ballistic missile preparedness drill with day shift officers by placing a call from a secure phone elsewhere in HIEMA to the State Warning Point. The recording that the midnight shift supervisor plays over the phone contains the text of an EAS message for a live ballistic missile alert, including the language, “this is not a drill,” instead of the language used in HIEMA’s standard operating procedure for this drill. Although the midnight shift officer’s recorded voice reads, “Exercise, Exercise, Exercise” at the beginning and end of the drill, using the phrase “this is not a drill” was a deviation from the drill procedure. [FCC-HI-2018#0084] Report and Recommendations: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency January 13, 2018 False Alert (p.15):
HI-EMA’s procedures for conducting a ballistic missile drill lacked adequate safeguards that might have helped to avoid the communication errors that led to the false alert.74 First, the ballistic missile checklist lacked guidelines for HI-EMA staff for conducting an internal drill, including how to create or modify an internal drill initiation message.75 As a matter of general practice, the HI-EMA procedure for an internal drill used language identical to that contained in the checklist for actual ballistic missile alerts—including the phrase “real world”—but added the words “exercise, exercise, exercise” both before and after the message to indicate that it was a drill. Use of the same language for both test and live alert initiation procedures could cause confusion among warning officers who received the message without prior notice, notwithstanding the statements at the beginning and end of the message that it was an exercise.

[TDRA-TS040#0002] Regulatory Update: New cell handset requirements in UAE (summary of TRA Technical Specification TS040) (requirement 3):
Message should be limited to 1 page maximum.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present with appropriate encodings (GSM-7 for English, UCS-2 for Arabic). However, neither version fits the UAE one-page limit: English is 3 pages and Arabic is 6. Neither text contains a protective action, so the first page carries the hazard but no action. Separately, the text contains both 'EXERCISE' and 'This is not a drill'. That contradiction is a content matter outside my delivery mandate and should be checked by the content reviewers.

objections.issue: Both language versions exceed the UAE one-page cell broadcast limit. English (GSM-7, 225 characters) is 3 pages and Arabic (UCS-2, 220 characters) is 6 pages. Content beyond page 1 may not be shown or may be truncated on handsets built to the UAE spec.
objections.fix: Cut each language to a single page: about 93 characters for English (GSM-7) and about 41 characters for Arabic (UCS-2). Keep the hazard, the area and the action, and drop secondary detail such as the visibility figure and coastal/inland wording. If a single-page Arabic text cannot carry hazard plus action, flag this for a human decision.
